newsitem.title: USA: H.B. Fuller Co raises qtly dividend.
newsitem.headline: H.B. Fuller Co raises qtly dividend.

text.p: H.B. Fuller Co chairman Anthony Andersen said Thursday its board of directors approved an increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.185 a share from $0.165 a share.
The dividend for the specialty chemical maker is payable May 12.

The record date dividend is April 28. Walter Kissling, chief executive officer, said revenue growth of six or seven percent this year was a possibility in the fiscal year ending in November. Company revenue hit $1.26 billion in fiscal 1996.

"That's still our goal," Kissling said following the company's annual shareholders meeting. "There's a good possibility (of reaching the goal). When we speak of seven percent that is internal growth. That has nothing to do with acquisitions."

Kissling added that operating expenses would increase for all of fiscal 1997 due to increased spending for research and development and information systems. Selling, administrative and other expenses decreased 0.5 percent to $323.5 million in fiscal 1996.

"We have as a goal to bring down operating expenses one- half of a percent a year as a percent of sales," he said. "But will total dollars decrease? No, because R&D and information system costs are growing."
At the meeting, a proposal to force the company to issue a report detailing its involvment in the tobacco industry was rejected, receiving only 9.53 percent of votes cast.
H.B. Fuller said in a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it's tobacco adhesives business was less than three percent of total sales.
